chunks: As for what Ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi al-Ward, who said:

I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a woman who is in the zuhr prayer and has prayed two rak'ahs, then she sees blood. He said: She rises from her place of prayer and does not make up the two rak'ahs. He said: And if she sees blood while she is in the maghrib prayer and has prayed two rak'ahs, then let her rise from her place of prayer, and when she becomes pure, let her make up the rak'ah that she missed from maghrib.

So what this report contains regarding the dropping of making up the two rak'ahs from the zuhr prayer is directed to one who entered the prayer at the beginning of its time, because one whose ruling is such is not considered negligent; and if she was not negligent, making it up is not binding upon her. And what it contains of the command to repeat the rak'ah from maghrib is directed to one who entered the prayer when the time had become constricted and then menstruated; then what she missed is binding upon her at that point. And that which indicates that this is directed to one who was negligent is that...

key_terms.تَضَيُّقِ ٱلْوَقْتِ: the constriction of prayer time near its end
key_terms.صَلَاةِ ٱلظُّهْرِ: the zuhr prayer in the specific case mentioned
key_terms.صَلَاةِ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib prayer in the parallel case
key_terms.فَرَّطَ: was negligent in delaying the prayer
key_terms.ٱلدَّمَ: the blood indicating the onset of menstruation
key_terms.ٱلْقَضَاءُ: making up a missed prayer or portion of it
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةِ: the woman whose legal ruling is being discussed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman begins prayer and then menstruation starts before she completes it?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for a woman who begins prayer and then menstruation starts during it. It distinguishes between cases in which makeup of the missed prayer is not required and cases in which part of the prayer must be made up, based on the timing of her entry into the prayer and whether there was negligence.
